subject: science
passage: The banyan, the national tree of India, grows in an unusual way. As its branches spread outward, they send down thin roots that hang in the air. When these roots reach the ground, they take hold in the soil and slowly thicken into woody pillars that look like extra trunks. Held up by these pillars, a single banyan can stretch its branches over a huge area.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To explain how the banyan tree is able to spread so widely
choices.B: To argue that the banyan is the most important tree in India
choices.C: To describe the many ways people have used banyan roots
choices.D: To describe how the banyan's roots look before they touch the soil

explanation.why: The text says the banyan "grows in an unusual way" and then traces the process: hanging roots reach the soil, become pillars, and hold up branches over "a huge area." The whole text explains how the tree manages to spread so far.
explanation.A: Correct. The text explains how hanging roots turn into supporting pillars that let the branches spread over a wide area.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text calls the banyan India's national tree but never argues that it is the most important tree.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text describes how the roots help the tree grow; it never mentions people using them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The hanging roots are only one stage in the process the text explains, not its main focus.
